For whatever it's worth, in a future version of the DevPool, @Draeieg and I envision a "betting market" where bounty hunters can get paid to provide time estimates down to the day (e.g. this bounty should take 3 days) and then those who answered the median will get paid from the losers. 
The objective is to incentivize more accurate time estimates for every task. This can be very useful for project managers who are not technical architects to create bounties and set priorities (and let the community figure out the timing) 
However I think that the bot would be parsing replies and then changing the label instead of the public bounty hunters still in this vision.

@0xcodercrane

Working alongside the "roles" idea (`billing_manager`, `member`, `admin`, `recruiting_manager` etc) we should be able to configure specific permissions on the user level for bot interactions and persist those to our database. To clarify, because "roles" are built into GitHub, those are useful for controlling GUI capabilities. The following refers to our custom capabilities via the bot.
- We need to intercept the "change label" event and check WHICH user is setting WHICH label in order to enforce this permissions system.
```
Roles
    Labels
        set priority
        set time
        set price
    Commands
        set payment multiplier
```
For each user we should be able to mark each list item prefixed with "set" as a boolean (true or false.) PER repository. Organization admins should automatically get full access control.
---
The purpose of this is to enable levels of delegation (and controlling funding from permits) within the organization, per repository. 
- It makes sense for technical talent to be able to review and edit bounties to provide a time estimate. 
- It makes sense for project managers to be able to assign a priority level.
- We don't have the #128 feature implemented yet, but my vision is to allow for direct price setting as well, which should have its own access control.
- #221 for context on the payment multiplier.
